title: Grateful Dead Live at Salt Palace on 1973-02-28

ai_review.summary: Solid soundboard capture of a high‑energy Feb ’73 show featuring a monster The Other One jam, tight Truckin’/Eyes sequence and standout performances from Jerry and Phil.
ai_review.review: The recording is a decent‑to‑good soundboard source that lets the band’s fire shine through.  Highlights include an extended, spacey The Other One, a powerful Truckin′→Too→Eyes>Dew stretch, and tight jams on He’s Gone, Row Jimmy and Sugar Magnolia.  While a few moments (e.g., Promised Land) are noted as slightly flubbed, the overall performance is energetic, cohesive, and highly recommended.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (many 5‑star comments) and note good soundboard quality; only a few moderate or negative remarks keep the rating just below top‑tier.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Not the sharpest board in the drawer but overall decent; many note clear, balanced sound (A+ on official release) with minor balance issues and occasional cuts.

standout_songs: Truckin' > The Other One > Eyes of the World > Dark Star (Dew)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set gels early and builds momentum; second set is a 2‑hour showcase with strong transitions, especially China>Jimmy and the extended Truckin′/Too/Eyes/Dew sequence.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His solos are repeatedly praised – a ‘perfect’ solo on Cold Rain & Snow and explosive blues‑scale work during the Truckin' jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Intro to The Other One described as loud/strong; Phil’s bass ‘bombs’ drive many jams, especially in the second set.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal work highlighted on Row Jimmy (harmonies) and his rhythm guitar support noted as solid.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s piano on El Paso called “pretty much perfect”; Donna Jean’s harmonies praised on Row Jimmy and He’s Gone.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming described as tight, energetic and a key part of the extended jams.
